title: While you're off Monday, fund a Roth
hook: Off Monday? Fund a Roth today.

concepts.title: The weekend timing: payroll gaps
concepts.body: If you're getting paid biweekly, three-day weekends are a hidden funding opportunity. The Labor Day paycheck still lands. The Roth contribution can be timed to coincide.

concepts.title: The 2026 limit: $7,500 ($8,600 at 50+)
concepts.body: The 2026 Roth IRA contribution limit is $7,500. Plus the $1,100 catch-up if you're fifty or older — total $8,600. The IRS deadline is your tax-filing deadline the following April, but funding early locks in the year's tax-free growth.

concepts.title: Time in market beats timing the market
concepts.body: Three days of growth on $7,500 at 7% real return is roughly $4.31. The dollar amount is small. The habit is everything — open the account, fund it, automate it. Don't touch it till fifty-nine and a half.

sources: IRS — 401(k) limit increases to $24,500 for 2026, IRA limit increases to $7,500 (IR-2025-111, Nov 13 2025)
IRS Pub 590-A — Roth IRA contribution limits
S&P 500 historical real return — 7% (Damodaran, NYU Stern, 2026 update)
